findings.text: follow-on: link_worker calls has_pending_link_work(state.facility) without path_prefixes (also at :1146 and again at the final pass), so a scoped run's link loop still detects facility-wide ingested-unlinked CodeFiles and drives link_code_evidence_to_signals over the whole facility; the phase gate at parallel.py:193 is scoped but this worker's own loop is not, so the scope promise the change makes in its docstring is not held for the link stage.

follow-on: the node added six tests in tests/graph/test_path_prefix_filter.py, but its recorded gate command is `pytest tests/discovery`, which does not select that directory, so those six tests ran under no gate in the run's own evidence and the helper's own unit tests are covered only by the transitive discovery tests.

follow-on: the run's gate log header names revision 8620aafc9, the base, while the reviewed head is bbbd783a, so the recorded green result is not keyed to the commit that landed; the worker ran the suite on the working tree before committing, and a run whose final commit is the change should log the gate at that head (the reviewer supplied both arms to close the gap).

follow-on: the reviewed manifest carries neither a baseline_suite nor an after_suite arm, so its own record holds no measured added-failure pair and the count had to be re-derived from arms the reviewer ran; recording the two suite fields would let the promotion audit read added failures without a second measurement.

item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is to make every discover code claim honour --path-prefix; the landed change threads the run's prefix list into the triage, enrichment, scoring and ingestion claims and the five has-work predicates in imas_codex/discovery/code/graph_ops.py and imas_codex/discovery/code/workers.py, so each claim filters on CodeFile.path and each phase gate ignores outside work; the one place left unscoped is link_worker, which still calls has_pending_link_work(state.facility) without the list.
item_verdicts.manifest: present and self-consistent (status complete, commit bbbd783a, changed_paths matching the diff, two gate logs named, negative-control note naming the checked mutation); one inaccuracy - it reports tests/discovery/test_code_claims_prefix_scope.py as 12 tests when the file holds 10, and it carries neither a baseline_suite nor an after_suite arm.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares eight write paths and the single commit bbbd783a touches exactly seven of them (four source files, two test files, one evidence fragment); the granted docs/figures directory is untouched, nothing outside the declared scope was written, and the reviewed worktree is clean.

justifications.durability: the scoping tests are sensitive to the defect they guard - the stub evaluates the query text it is handed, so dropping a claim's {prefix_clause} makes that claim return the outside row and reddens its test, as I confirmed for the ingest claim by reproducing the mutation; one assertion is weaker, tests/graph/test_path_prefix_filter.py:16-18 compares the helper's clause against render_path_prefix_clause("sf", "prefixes"), the very call the implementation makes, so it holds by construction and pins delegation rather than behaviour.
justifications.evidence: I read the recorded gate and reproduced both arms in scratch trees - base 8620aafc9 tests/discovery 1167 passed EXIT=0, head bbbd783a 1177 passed EXIT=0, zero FAILED ids on either side - and reproduction of the declared mutation (the {prefix_clause} line removed from the ingest claim at workers.py:570) leaves the outside file claimed and fails tests/discovery/test_code_claims_prefix_scope.py::TestClaimsHonourPrefix::test_ingest_claim_ignores_files_outside_the_prefix, EXIT=1; deduction because the run's own gate log header names revision 8620aafc9, not the reviewed head, so its recorded result is not tied to the commit that landed.
justifications.fit: build_path_prefix_filter sits beside render_path_prefix_clause in imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py:281, the docstrings name the mechanism (the value travels with the predicate) rather than a plan item, the commit subject and body are conventional with no plan, ticket or phase identifier and no AI attribution, and the single-commit change leaves the surrounding claim style intact.
justifications.goal_fidelity: imas_codex/discovery/code/graph_ops.py:304-744 applies build_path_prefix_filter to the triage, enrich, score, scan and five has-work predicates on CodeFile.path and FacilityPath.path, and imas_codex/discovery/code/workers.py:566 applies it to the ingest claim, so every claim the goal names honours the scope; deduction only because imas_codex/discovery/code/workers.py:1102 leaves the link worker's own has-work call unscoped, so a scoped run's link loop still sees facility-wide ingested-unlinked files.
justifications.reuse: imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py:298 wraps the existing render_path_prefix_clause owner instead of forking it, and every claim and predicate that previously hand-rolled `if path_prefixes: prefix_clause = render_path_prefix_clause(...)` now calls the one helper, so the capability has a single owner and the before-duplication is removed.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff of bbbd783a touches only imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py, imas_codex/discovery/code/graph_ops.py, imas_codex/discovery/code/workers.py, imas_codex/discovery/code/parallel.py, the two test files and docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-discovery-completion/code-claims-honour-prefix.html, all inside the declared write paths, with the granted figures directory unused and the worktree clean.
